title: Screen time & digital wellbeing
examples: What is the best amount of screen time for my age?
How does looking at screens affect my sleep?
Can you suggest some good habits for digital wellbeing?

explain.say: We are learning about healthy habits for our digital lives today.
One good habit is putting your phone away before bed time.
Another habit is taking a short break every hour when you study.
We must also think about how screen time affects our sleep quality.
When we use screens late, the blue light can trick our brains.
In real life, setting a 'digital curfew' is a great habit to try.

faq.q: Does looking at screens really mess up my sleep?
faq.a: Yes, the light from screens can interfere with the natural sleep hormones your body needs. This makes it harder for you to fall asleep at the right time.
asks: Why do screens keep me awake?
What is the link between phones and sleep?

faq.q: How long should I take breaks from my phone?
faq.a: Experts suggest taking a short break, maybe for ten minutes, every hour you spend looking at a screen. This helps your eyes and brain rest.
asks: What is a good break time?
When should I stop using my phone?

faq.q: What is 'blue light' and why is it bad?
faq.a: Blue light is a type of visible light emitted by many screens. It can signal to your brain that it is daytime, even when it is dark.
asks: What is the danger of blue light?
Does blue light keep me awake?

faq.q: Are there specific times I should stop using devices?
faq.a: It is generally recommended to stop using bright screens at least one hour before you plan to go to sleep. This helps your body prepare for rest.
asks: What is the best time to put my phone down?
How far before sleep should I stop screens?

faq.q: Does reading a physical book help with digital wellbeing?
faq.a: Yes, reading a physical book uses different parts of your brain than looking at a screen. It helps you disconnect and relax properly.
asks: What is a good alternative to screens?
Can I read a book instead of my phone?

facts: Blue light from screens can suppress melatonin, the sleep hormone.
Taking regular breaks helps reduce eye strain from screens.
Establishing a device-free time before bed improves sleep quality.
Good digital habits help maintain a healthy balance in daily life.

quiz.say: To improve sleep, it is best to stop using bright screens:

options.show: Right before turning off the light
options.say: Right before turning off the light

quiz.why: This allows your body's natural sleep hormones time to increase.

wrong.0: This is too close to sleep and the blue light will still be too strong.
wrong.1: Waiting until you feel tired means you might already have poor sleep habits.
wrong.2: Healthy habits need to be practiced every day, not just on certain days.

quiz.say: What is the best action to take every hour of screen time?

options.show: Check social media for five minutes
options.say: Check social media for five minutes

options.show: Drink a large amount of water
options.say: Drink a large amount of water

quiz.why: Moving around helps your eyes and body reset after focusing on a screen.

wrong.0: This leads to eye strain and can make you feel more tired later.
wrong.2: This keeps your eyes focused on a screen, which defeats the purpose of a break.
wrong.3: Drinking water is good, but it does not replace the need to move your body.

quiz.say: If you want to improve your sleep, which habit is most important?

options.show: Only limiting phone use on weekdays
options.say: Only limiting phone use on weekdays

quiz.why: Routine signals to your brain that it is time to wind down for sleep.

wrong.1: Weekends are also important for maintaining healthy habits.
wrong.2: The routine should include more than just reading, like dim lights.
wrong.3: While blue light is bad, a full routine includes relaxation steps too.
